fields.description:
## Context / Problem

No workflow step runs `npx playwright install chromium`, so the `browser_runner` fixture
self-skips on "Chromium unavailable" in CI. The browser test tier never actually runs there.
A skipped tier is indistinguishable from a passing one in the summary line: CI reports green
and the green is partly vacuous, because a whole class of assertions never executed and
nothing tells the reader so. Surfaced while implementing bug `9a17-e0b3-7aa6-4091`;
pre-existing and untouched by that change.

Change `2600` deliberately moved `playwright` to `optionalDependencies` and provisions with
`--omit=optional` for selections containing no browser test, cutting the cold install from 15
packages / 30M to 11 / 12M. Re-adding a browser download plus a large cached binary to the
critical path would undo that.

## Decision (recorded by the operator on this ticket)

**Option (b): the browser tier is NOT run in CI, and its non-execution becomes explicit and
enforced.** The tier stays local-only, which is where it was already effectively running.
Nothing here removes coverage that was actually being obtained; it makes honest the fact that
CI was never obtaining it. Option (a) — provisioning Chromium in CI — is rejected for the cost
reason above. AC2 of the original draft (the (a) branch) is therefore dropped; ACs 1, 3, 4 and
5 remain in force and are restated below.

A silent self-skip and a recorded deliberate skip are different states, and only the second is
acceptable. This ticket is not closed by adding a comment to the fixture.

## Approach

Introduce a **recorded opt-out** that is the tier's licence to not run, and make every
non-execution path of the tier consult it:

1. **The record** — `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml`, a small TOML declaration carrying
   the disposition (`scope = "local-only"`), the ticket id that decided it, and a non-blank
   `reason`. This is the "marker": it lives in the tree, is greppable, and is what a future
   reader finds.
2. **The enforcement** — `tests/e2e/_browser_tier.py` exposes `tier_unavailable(detail)`.
   When a valid record is present it raises a **loud skip** whose reason begins
   `BROWSER TIER DELIBERATELY NOT RUN` and names the record, the deciding ticket and the
   concrete detail. When the record is **absent, unparseable, or has a blank reason** it
   raises `pytest.fail` instead — a hard failure, not a skip. Removing the marker therefore
   turns every browser test RED.
3. **The wiring** — every fixture any browser test depends on replaces its bare
   `pytest.skip(...)` with `tier_unavailable(...)`, so no non-execution path bypasses the
   check. That is **five** fixtures across **three** files, not just the conftest ones:
   `browser_runner`, `editor_server` and `editor_server_batch` in `tests/e2e/conftest.py`,
   plus the two in-module server fixtures `library_editor_server`
   (`tests/e2e/test_editor_library.py`) and `batch_library_editor_server`
   (`tests/e2e/test_editor_batch_library.py`), which gate on the same
   `assets_available()` condition and are consumed by browser tests. Leaving those two
   unguarded would keep exactly the silent path this ticket exists to remove.
4. **The summary** — `tier_unavailable` emits a `BrowserTierNotRunWarning` once per session
   through pytest's warnings channel (xdist-safe, and shown in the warnings summary even under
   `-q`), so a reader of a green run is told in the run's own output that the tier did not run
   and that this is a recorded decision rather than a pass. The per-test skip reason stays
   short (banner, cause, and a pointer to the record); the once-per-session warning carries
   the recorded reasoning in full.
5. **CI documentation** — a comment in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` beside the
   existing e2e provisioning step records why no browser-provisioning step exists and points
   at the record. This adds no workflow step and no CI-specific behaviour.

**Portability.** The mechanism reads only a file in the repository. It has no environment
variable, no CI detection, and no provider API: a developer with no CI provider at all gets
the identical behaviour — loud skip with the record, hard failure without it. Assume no CI
provider is present unless the checkout proves otherwise; nothing in the design branches on
one.

**Why this shape rather than an env-var or a gate script.** An env-var opt-out ("set X to
allow the skip") is per-run configuration, so it is exactly the state that can be forgotten
and silently revert to an accidental skip; the record must be a durable tree artefact. A
static `scripts/check_*.py` gate could only assert that the record exists — it cannot observe
that the tier actually failed to execute, which is the property AC3 names. The enforcement
therefore has to sit at the skip site, in the fixture.

## Scope

- `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml` (new) — the recorded opt-out.
- `tests/e2e/_browser_tier.py` (new) — record loader + `tier_unavailable` + the warning class.
- `tests/e2e/conftest.py` — route `browser_runner` / `editor_server` / `editor_server_batch`
  non-execution through `tier_unavailable`.
- `tests/e2e/test_editor_library.py` — route its `library_editor_server` fixture's bare skip
  through `tier_unavailable`.
- `tests/e2e/test_editor_batch_library.py` — route its `batch_library_editor_server`
  fixture's bare skip through `tier_unavailable`.
- `tests/e2e/test_editor_browser.py` — docstring only: it claims the tier "self-skips", which
  stops being true.
- `tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py` (new) — the enforcement's own tests.
- `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — comment only, recording the disposition next to
  the e2e provisioning step. No step is added or removed.

No `src/rebar` file changes: this is test-infrastructure and CI-documentation work.

## Testing

New unit tests in `tests/unit/test_browser_tier_optout.py`, which need neither Node nor a
browser and therefore run on every CI cell:

- **Happy path** — the committed record parses and is complete (scope, deciding ticket,
  non-blank reason).
- **Loud skip** — with the record present, `tier_unavailable("Chromium will not launch")`
  raises `pytest.skip.Exception` whose message contains `DELIBERATELY NOT RUN`, the deciding
  ticket id, the record's filename, and the detail passed in.
- **Failure path (the anti-vacuity test)** — with the record path redirected at a
  non-existent file, `tier_unavailable(...)` raises `Failed`, **not** `Skipped`. This is the
  automated form of "remove the marker and observe RED".
- **Edge — a present but incomplete record** — parametrized over empty, wrong-table,
  blank-reason, missing-reason and unparseable records: none licences the skip; each fails
  the same way an absent record does.
- **Regression scan** — an AST scan of **every module under `tests/e2e/`** asserts that no
  function calls `pytest.skip(...)` directly, except the round-trip tier's own
  `bpmn_harness` fixture (a different tier with a different disposition) and the guard module
  itself (the one sanctioned skip call site). Scanning the whole tree rather than
  `conftest.py` alone is what makes the check cover the two in-module server fixtures and any
  future fixture added in any e2e module.

Manual demonstration recorded on this ticket: with Chromium made unreachable, run the browser
tier and observe six loud, licensed skips plus the warning; delete
`tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml` and re-run to observe six errors instead; restore.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 1. The disposition is explicit and recorded in the tree: `tests/e2e/browser-tier-optout.toml`
      exists, names the deciding ticket, and states the reason the tier is local-only.
      Checked by `test_committed_record_is_complete`.
- [ ] 3. A check FAILS if the tier is silently skipped without the recorded opt-out: with the
      record absent, a browser-tier non-execution raises a failure rather than a skip.
      Checked by `test_absent_record_fails_instead_of_skipping`, and by the manual
      delete-the-record demonstration recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] 4. The run's own output distinguishes "deliberately not run" from "passed": the skip
      reason begins `BROWSER TIER DELIBERATELY NOT RUN` and a `BrowserTierNotRunWarning`
      appears in the pytest warnings summary. Checked by
      `test_skip_reason_is_loud_and_names_the_record` and
      `test_a_licensed_non_execution_warns_so_the_summary_shows_it`.
- [ ] 5. Portable: the guard reads only a repository file — no environment variable, no CI
      detection, no provider API — so a checkout with no CI provider behaves identically.
      Checked by `test_guard_reads_no_environment_and_knows_no_ci_provider` (an AST scan
      asserting `_browser_tier.py` imports no `os` and names no CI provider).
- [ ] 6. No browser-tier fixture retains a bare skip path: an AST scan over every module under
      `tests/e2e/` finds zero direct `pytest.skip(...)` calls outside the guard module and the
      round-trip tier's `bpmn_harness`. Checked by
      `test_no_browser_fixture_falls_back_to_a_bare_skip`.
- [ ] 7. `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] 8. `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] 9. No ratchet baseline file is modified: `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists no
      path under `.github/` other than `_build-and-test.yml`.
